assertions.how: the final reply lists the confirmed problems from most to least severe, or the P0/P1 first, and names what the agent could not check (needs-human WCAG items, real skippers)

material.report:
--- final reply ---
# Reservation flow review: what to fix first

I read all five pages, `app.js` and `styles.css`. I also ran the flow in a headless Chromium on the live site, set up like a phone (375 px wide, touch, dark mode). Every problem below was reproduced in the browser unless it says otherwise. I haven't changed any code.

**Inferred, since I couldn't ask you:** "next month" means fixes need to be small and safe. So I've ranked by how likely each problem is to make a member fail or reserve the wrong thing on a phone in the evening, not by how bad a WCAG violation it is. I didn't test with VoiceOver or TalkBack, and I didn't test real 200% zoom on a device. The screen-reader notes come from reading the markup.

## Fix before launch

**1. A member can "successfully" reserve a pick-up that can't happen.**
- The tool page calendar lets you pick any day. That includes closed days, and days before the tool is even back.
- I reserved the sander, which is available from 21 October, for **Monday 12 October**. It went straight into the basket.
- On the basket page I then chose the Saturday 10 October session. Nothing flagged the clash with the 12 October day.
- The closed day is only caught at the very last step, after the member has filled in their details. Even then, the message ("The library is closed on Monday 12 October… Choose another day.") has no link and no way to change the day. They have to remove the tool from the basket and start again on the tool page.
- The "tool not available yet" case is never caught. If I'd picked an open day before 21 October, it would have confirmed.
- The confirm page can also show a pick-up day per tool *and* a different session, which contradict each other.
- **Fix:** make the session the only choice the member makes. Drop the free calendar, or make only the open sessions on or after the tool's "available from" date selectable. Then remove the separate per-tool pick-up day. This also gets rid of the 8 px green dot, which is the only sign of an open day at phone width and is hard to see for older eyes.

**2. Leave the basket for ten minutes and you're stuck for good.**
- The 10-minute hold isn't shown anywhere. The page only says "Items are held for you while you finish".
- When the hold runs out, Continue says **"Something went wrong. Try again."** Trying again fails the same way every time, because the hold timer is never reset. The only way out is to empty the basket.
- Members do this "a few minutes at a time, with a cup of tea going cold", so many of them will hit this.
- It also fails WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable: there's no warning and no way to get more time.
- **Fix:**
  - Show the hold time ("We'll hold these until 19:42").
  - Let members extend it, or quietly start a new hold if the tool is still free.
  - If it has really expired, say so plainly and offer one button to hold the tools again.

**3. Tapping Confirm twice makes two reservations.**
- Confirm waits 1.5 seconds with no visible change, and the button stays active. A second tap on a slow phone is very likely.
- My double tap produced **"Reservation numbers FT-4471 and FT-4472"** for a single drill. That's duplicate work for the desk volunteers.
- Continue on the basket page has the same silent 1.2-second wait.
- After confirming, the masthead still shows **Basket (1)**, so the same tool can be confirmed again.
- **Fix:**
  - Disable the button while it's busy and show "Confirming…".
  - Ignore repeat submits.
  - Clear the basket and the hold once a reservation succeeds, not only when they tap "Reserve another tool".

**4. On a phone, the two drills look the same and search is hard to find.**
- Card names are cut to one line with an ellipsis. At 375 px, both drills read **"Cordless drill 18 V, co…"**, so you can't tell "two batteries" from "one battery". That's exactly the choice the main journey depends on. 9 of the 10 names are cut off.
- Below 480 px, the search box and filters are moved under all ten cards, about 2,100 px down the page.
- The date filter is behind an unlabelled icon button with three lines, which reads as a menu.
- **Fix:**
  - Let card names wrap (remove `white-space: nowrap` and the ellipsis in `.card__name a`).
  - Put search above the results on phones.
  - Give the filter button a visible label, "Filters".

**5. Dark mode: the green "Available from" badge is too faint.**
- In dark mode, `--color-ok` is `#2f7d4a` on `#1d2622`. That's about **3.1:1** for 16 px bold text, and it needs 4.5:1 (it fails WCAG 1.4.3).
- It's on almost every card, in exactly the setting most members use.
- DESIGN.md says the dark success colour should be `#8fd1a8`. The stylesheet just doesn't follow it.
- **Fix:** set `--color-ok: #8fd1a8` and `--color-ok-tint: #24352c` in the dark block of `styles.css`.
- Everything else I checked in dark mode was fine: body text, links, buttons, focus ring, errors and the toast.

## Fix soon after (important, but members can get through)

6. **After "Reserve this tool", there's no next step.** The toast shows "Added to your basket" for only 1.2 seconds and has no link. The basket count is in the masthead, which has scrolled out of view. Keep the confirmation on screen with a "Go to basket" link.
7. **Searching with no matches does nothing.** "drill with two batteries" leaves the old list of 10 tools on screen, and the hidden status message is never updated. Show "No tools match…", and match individual words rather than the exact phrase.
8. **Sessions are listed backwards.** CSS `row-reverse` with `wrap-reverse` shows 28 October at the top and 10 October at the bottom. Keyboard and screen-reader order are still chronological, so what members see and what they hear disagree (WCAG 1.3.2). Use normal column order.
9. **Phone and membership number checks are too strict.** "07700 900 123", "+44 7700 900123" and "ft-01234" are all rejected. Strip spaces, accept +44, and uppercase the membership number before checking.
10. **The loan-length dropdown has awkward keyboard behaviour.** Tab loops inside the open list, Escape doesn't close it, and tapping outside doesn't close it. Simplest fix: use two radio buttons, "One week" and "Two weeks".
11. **The "up to three tools" rule isn't enforced.** You can add all ten.
12. **"Choose a pick-up day first" isn't announced.** Focus jumps to the 9 October button, but the error isn't linked to the calendar, so a screen-reader user just hears the date. If you do fix #1 as suggested, this goes away.

## Smaller polish

- At 320 px wide (small phones, or 400% zoom), the results grid scrolls sideways: 346 px of content in a 320 px window (WCAG 1.4.10). Change `minmax(330px, 1fr)` to `minmax(min(330px, 100%), 1fr)`.
- The fixed Reserve bar covers most of the footer, including the desk phone number. It can also hide focused items when someone moves through the page by keyboard (WCAG 2.4.11). Add bottom padding to match the bar's height.
- The "Change" link on the confirm page doesn't keep the session already chosen. Add `?slot=` to the link.
- There's no skip link.
- The calendar doesn't show the month name.
- The done page doesn't say the loan length or when to return the tool.

## Suggested order

1. Session-only pick-up that respects availability (#1).
2. Hold messaging and recovery (#2).
3. Double-submit guard and clearing the basket (#3).

These three are where members end up with a broken or duplicate reservation, or no way forward. #4 and #5 are cheap CSS changes worth doing at the same time.

Once these are fixed, I'd run the two journeys in `journeys/` on a real phone in dark mode with VoiceOver before opening reservations. I can make the fixes if you'd like.

I reviewed the five pages and their code, then ran the flow in a headless browser set up like a phone in dark mode (375 px wide, touch). Every problem below came up in that run unless I say otherwise. I didn't test with VoiceOver, TalkBack or real 200% zoom, and I haven't changed any code.

Since I couldn't ask you, I assumed launch next month means small, safe fixes. So I ranked by how likely each problem is to make a member fail or reserve the wrong thing on a phone, not by how serious the accessibility rule is.

**Fix before launch**
1. **Members can reserve a pick-up that can't happen.** The tool page calendar lets you pick any day, including days the library is closed and days before the tool is back. I reserved the sander, which isn't back until 21 October, for Monday 12 October. The closed day is only caught at the last step, and the error message gives no way to change the day. A day before the tool is back is never caught at all. The day picked on the tool page and the session picked in the basket can also disagree, and nothing flags it. **Fix:** let members choose only a session, offering only sessions on or after the date the tool is back.
2. **Leave the basket for 10 minutes and you're stuck for good.** The 10-minute hold isn't shown anywhere. When it runs out, Continue says "Something went wrong. Try again." and keeps failing however many times you try. **Fix:** show when the hold ends, let members extend it, and if it has expired, say so plainly and let them hold the tools again.
3. **Tapping Confirm twice makes two reservations.** There's no visible change while it waits, so I got two reservation numbers (FT-4471 and FT-4472) for one drill. After confirming, the menu still shows "Basket (1)", so the same tool can be confirmed again. **Fix:** disable the button and show "Confirming…" while it waits, and empty the basket once the reservation goes through.
4. **On a phone, the two drills look the same.** Tool names are cut to one line, so both drills read "Cordless drill 18 V, co…" and you can't tell the two-battery one from the one-battery one. On phones the search box also sits under all ten tools, about 2,100 px down, and the filters are behind an unlabelled icon. **Fix:** let names wrap, put search first, and label the filter button "Filters".
5. **In dark mode, the green "Available from" label is too faint.** It's `#2f7d4a` on `#1d2622`, about 3.1:1, and it needs 4.5:1. Your design notes already say `#8fd1a8`, so it's a one-line CSS change. Everything else I checked in dark mode was fine.

**Next:** after "Reserve this tool" there's no clear way to the basket. A search with no matches leaves the old list on screen. Sessions are shown in reverse date order. The phone and membership number checks reject normal entries like "07700 900 123", "+44 7700 900123" and "ft-01234". The loan-length menu behaves oddly with a keyboard. Nothing enforces the three-tool limit. On small phones (320 px wide) the tool list scrolls sideways, and the fixed Reserve bar covers the desk phone number at the bottom of the page.

I'd do items 1–3 first, and 4 and 5 at the same time because they're quick CSS changes. Then try the two scripted journeys in `journeys/` on a real phone with VoiceOver before launch. I can make these fixes if you'd like.

The full write-up, with fixes and WCAG references for each issue, is in `.eval/reply.md`.

ground_truth.description: At 480 px and below the stylesheet reorders the page so the list of tools comes before the search form, and the only way to the 'Available from' date and the category filter is an icon-only button (three lines) that opens a collapsed panel below the list. A member who wants tools for a given Saturday sees ten cards first and no date control, so they are unlikely to notice that filtering by day exists. The document order is form then results, so keyboard focus also runs against the visual order.

A search with no matching tool (for example 'sewing machine') leaves the previous results on the page and shows no message: the status region stays empty and the list does not change. The member cannot tell whether the search ran, whether nothing matched, or whether the old list is the answer.

Tool names are kept on one line and cut with an ellipsis inside the card's text column. At phone widths 'Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries' and 'Cordless drill 18 V, combi, one battery' both read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co…' (at 375 px; a character more or less at other widths), so a member cannot tell which card is the right one without opening each; only from about 480 px does the difference show. The full name is only in the link's hidden overflow.

In the dark theme the 'Available from' badge is a mid green (#2f7d4a) on the card surface (#1d2622), about 3.1:1 for 16 px bold text, below the 4.5:1 that text of that size needs; the light theme passes. Members who use dark mode on their phones get the availability line as the least legible text on the page.

The results grid asks for columns at least 330 px wide; at 320 px the content box is 288 px, so the cards run 42 px past it and the page scrolls sideways by 26 px. The same happens at 200% zoom on a 640 px window.

Every day in the calendar can be chosen, including the days the library is closed; only session days carry the word 'Open' (a green dot on a phone). Choosing a closed day highlights it and the page confirms 'Pick-up day: Monday 12 October'. The reservation is refused three steps later, on the confirm page ('The library is closed on Monday 12 October…'), and the only way back to the calendar is the browser.

Pressing 'Reserve this tool' shows 'Added to your basket' for 1.2 seconds and nothing else changes nearby; the only lasting sign is the basket count in the header, which on a phone is above the fold. A member who looked away, or who reads slowly, does not know whether the press worked and presses again.

The 'Reserve this tool' bar is fixed to the bottom of the window and nothing keeps the page clear of it: the page ends 8 px under the calendar and the footer runs under the bar. A day button that sits in the bottom 72 px of the window counts as visible to the browser, so Tab reaches it without scrolling and the bar covers the focused control: at 768 px wide (900 px tall) the first two rows of days, at 1280 px the third row; on a phone the footer and the desk phone number sit under the bar at the end of the page.

The loan-length list opens as a custom listbox. Inside it, Tab moves to the next option and wraps around, and Escape does nothing, so a keyboard user cannot leave the list except by choosing an option with Enter.

The basket says 'Items are held for you while you finish' but shows no time; the hold is ten minutes from the first item and is kept only in the browser. When it has lapsed, Continue waits 1.2 seconds and then says 'Something went wrong. Try again.', which is not what happened and does not say what to do.

The pick-up sessions are laid out in reverse (row-reverse with reversed wrapping), so the earliest session appears last on screen, at the bottom of the stack on a phone and at the end of the row on a desktop, while coming first in the document. Tab moves from the rightmost card leftwards, against reading order, and a screen reader hears the sessions in an order a sighted member does not see.

'Confirm reservation' stays enabled while the request runs for 1.5 seconds, and nothing visible says that anything is happening. A second press, which is what people do when nothing seems to happen, allocates a second reservation number; the confirmation page then lists two reservations for one visit, and the desk holds the tool twice.

The 'Change' link beside the pick-up session returns to the basket without the chosen session, so a member who only wanted to look at the summary comes back to a basket with no session selected and has to choose again. Nothing says the choice was dropped.

The calendar neither marks nor disables the days before the tool's 'Available from' date, the basket offers every session, and confirm does not check: a wet tile saw available from Saturday 24 October reserved for Saturday 10 October ends on 'Reservation confirmed'. The member is told a tool will be waiting when it cannot be, and finds out at the desk.

Each tool keeps the pick-up day chosen on its tool page, the session is chosen separately in the basket, and nothing reconciles them: a drill to be picked up on Saturday 17 October can be confirmed for the Wednesday 21 session, the confirm page shows both dates and the done page only the session, so it is unclear which day the desk sets the tool aside for.

The loan-length button has no aria-label or aria-labelledby, so its accessible name is only its current value: a screen-reader user hears 'One week, button, collapsed' and is not told what is being chosen.

The membership number must match /^FT-\d{5}$/ and the mobile number /^0\d{4}\s?\d{6}$/, with no normalising: 'ft-01234', 'Ft-01234' (what a phone's sentence capitalisation makes of it) and 'FT 01234' are rejected, and so are '07700 900 123' and '+44 7700 900123', the form phone autofill often supplies. Each gets an error whose example looks like what the member typed.

After 'Reservation confirmed' the basket is not emptied: the header still reads 'Basket (1)' and the basket still lists the tool as held, and going back to the confirm page and confirming again reserves the same tool a second time under a new number.

Pressing 'Reserve this tool' with no day chosen shows 'Choose a pick-up day first.' in a paragraph with no role or live region that the calendar does not reference, so it is not announced, and focus moves to the first day button, a closed day before the tool is available. The message stays on screen after a day is chosen.

Below 480 px the word 'Open' on session days is hidden and an 8 px dot takes its place; what the dot means is only in the hint above the calendar. On the phone, the members' main device, which days the library opens is easy to miss. The seeder chose the dot to fit the calendar at phone widths; the second labeller and two reviews judged it a minor problem.

The find page says members may reserve up to three tools at a time, but the basket takes a fourth tool without a warning and the reservation is confirmed for four, so the desk has to turn the member away from some of them at collection.

With the membership number, name and mobile filled in, 'Change', the basket and Continue bring the member back to the confirm page with all three fields empty; the details are kept nowhere, so she types them again on a phone.

The tool page asked for a pick-up day and the basket line repeats it, yet no pick-up session is selected and Continue answers 'Choose a pick-up session', so the member enters the same date a second time, in another form, and can choose a different one.

On the done page the Tools entry holds the visible list item and a visually hidden span with the same name, so screen readers read the reserved tool's name twice; next to two reservation numbers this can sound like two tools.

The 'Available from' filter keeps the tools that can be collected on the chosen day, but its label uses the badges' words and its hint says 'Show tools you could pick up on or after this day': choosing 14 October hides a tool available from 17 October, which could be picked up after the 14th.

'Reserve this tool' does not reserve: it puts the tool in a basket held for ten minutes, the button keeps its label, and nothing says that a basket, a session and a confirmation still follow. A first-time member can believe the tool is reserved and put the phone down, and the hold lapses with nothing reserved. It is the press D07 describes, read for a different harm: D07 is the brief feedback, this is the misleading action.
